# Jubilees Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Prologue — God Speaks to Moses on Sinai

---

**1:1** In the first year after Israel left Egypt — on the sixteenth day of the third month — God called to Moses: "Come up to me on the mountain. I have written the law and its commands on two stone tablets, and I am going to give them to you so that you can teach the people."

**1:2** Moses climbed God's mountain. The glory of the LORD descended on Mount Sinai, and a cloud wrapped around it for six days.

**1:3** On the seventh day, God called out to Moses from inside the cloud. From the mountain's peak, his glory blazed like fire.

**1:4** Moses stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights while God taught him everything — the whole story from beginning to end — the entire calendar of the law and its testimony.

**1:5** God said: "Listen carefully to everything I tell you today. Write it all in a book, so that future generations can see for themselves that I never abandoned my people — even though they kept breaking the covenant I am making with you today here on Sinai."

**1:6** "When all these troubles come on them, they will finally understand that I have always been right, and that I have always been there with them."

**1:7** "Write down every word I give you today. I already know how stubborn and rebellious they are — even before I bring them into the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the land overflowing with milk and honey."

**1:8** "They will eat well and grow comfortable, and then they will walk away from me to worship gods that cannot save them from any disaster. And everything written here will stand as evidence against them."

**1:9** "They will forget every command I give them and go chasing after the nations — their filth, their shameful rites, their gods. And those gods will destroy them: a trap, a torment, a slow ruin."

**1:10** "Many will die. Many will be captured and handed over to their enemies, because they threw away my laws and my appointed times — my sabbaths, my sacred festivals, my sanctuary, my very name that rested over them."

**1:11** "They will build shrines on hilltops, set up sacred pillars, carve out idols, and bow down to the things their own hands made. Those idols will be their downfall."

**1:12** "I will send prophets to warn them, and they will not listen. They will kill those prophets too, and hunt down anyone who tries to live by the law. They will tear everything apart and do the worst evil imaginable in my sight."

**1:13** "So I will turn my face away from them. I will hand them over to foreign nations — to be enslaved, plundered, and destroyed. I will drive them out of the land and scatter them to the ends of the earth."

**1:14** "They will forget my entire law — all my commands, all my statutes. They will lose track of the calendar: the new moons, the sabbaths, the festivals, the jubilees."

**1:15** "But one day they will come back to me — from every nation, with everything they have, heart and soul. I will bring them all home. They will search for me, and they will find me, because they will be searching with everything in them."

**1:16** "I will pour out peace over them beyond measure. I will plant them again like a righteous garden, with my whole heart and soul. They will be a blessing, not a curse. They will rise, not fall."

**1:17** "I will build my temple right in the middle of them. I will live among them. I will be their God, and they will truly be my people."

**1:18** "I will never abandon them, never push them away. I am the LORD their God."

**1:19** Moses pressed his face to the ground and prayed: "LORD my God — don't abandon your people, your own inheritance. Don't let them stumble through life in delusion. Don't hand them over to the nations that will enslave them and drag them away from you."

**1:20** "Show your people mercy, LORD. Give them a spirit that holds straight. Don't let Beliar — that spirit of accusation — rule over them, drag them into court before you, and lead them off every righteous path until they're lost from your sight entirely."

**1:21** "These are your people — your own heritage — the ones you pulled out of Egypt with your mighty hand. Give them clean hearts and a holy spirit. Don't let them keep falling into sin, now and forever."

**1:22** The LORD replied to Moses: "I know exactly how contrary, stubborn, and willful they are. They will not listen — not until they finally face their own sin and their ancestors' sin head-on."

**1:23** "But when that happens, they will come back to me wholeheartedly — with everything in them. I will cut away the hardness around their hearts and the hearts of their children. I will give them a holy spirit and make them clean, and they will never turn away from me again — not from that day on, not ever."

**1:24** "They will cling to me and live by all my commands. They will follow through, and I will be their Father — and they will be my children."

**1:25** "Every one of them will be called a child of the living God. Every angel and every spirit will know — they will all know — that these are my children and I am their Father, and that I love them, truly and rightly."

**1:26** "Write it all down for Moses — everything I'm telling you — from the very beginning to the very end. Everything that will happen through all the ages — through the law and the testimony, through the weeks and the jubilees — until the day I come down and live among them forever."

**1:27** Then God spoke to the angel of the presence: "Start from the creation and write it all out for Moses — all the way until the day my sanctuary stands among them permanently."

**1:28** "The LORD will show himself to the whole world, and everyone will know: I am the God of Israel, Father of all Jacob's children, and King on Mount Zion forever. Zion and Jerusalem will be holy."

**1:29** So the angel of the presence — the one who had marched ahead of Israel through the wilderness — took up the tablets that recorded all the divisions of time, from creation onward, through the jubilees and the years. And he told Moses everything: every detail of the law, the testimony, the calendar — all of it, until the whole story was told.

---
*PNEUMA notes: "Beliar" (v.20) retained as proper name — too theologically specific to paraphrase. "Plant of righteousness" rendered as "righteous garden" to convey the agricultural metaphor. "Angel of the presence" retained as honorific title.*
